title: Fire & Smoke Damage Restoration in Phoenix, AZ | Gold Water Fire
description: Fire and smoke damage restoration across the Phoenix metro: board-up, soot and odor removal, water from the hoses, and the full rebuild. Call (480) 999-3339, 24/7.
h1: Fire and smoke damage restoration in the Phoenix metro
intro: After a fire, the house you knew is suddenly a place you are not sure you can walk into. You are not supposed to know what comes next. One step at a time is enough.

photo.alt: Fire damage restoration crew removing smoke-damaged drywall near a soot-covered brick fireplace

bottomLine: Stay out until the fire department says the house is safe, then call your insurer and get the property secured. Smoke reaches far past the burned room, so the cleanup plan comes from a walk-through of the whole house, not just what is black.
plainEnglishBody: Smoke damage cleanup is removing the soot and smoke residue a fire leaves on walls, ceilings, ductwork and belongings, then treating the odor at its source. Different fires leave different residue, so the cleaning method changes with what burned. Odor is handled last, once the residue that carries it is gone.
whyItMattersHeading: Why smoke matters even where nothing burned
whyItMattersBody: Smoke follows air. It moves through the HVAC system and into closets, attic insulation and rooms the fire never reached, which is why a house can smell of smoke weeks later. Residue left on surfaces stains and sets in the longer it sits, so the sooner it is cleaned, the more can be cleaned instead of replaced.

causes.heading: Kitchen fires
causes.body: Grease and cooking fires leave a thin, sticky residue with a strong odor that coats cabinets and walls well beyond the stove.

causes.heading: Electrical and appliance fires
causes.body: Wiring, dryers, attic fans and charging batteries can start a fire inside a wall or attic, out of sight.

causes.heading: Garage fires
causes.body: Fuel, chemicals and stored contents burn hot, and smoke often reaches the house through the shared wall and doorway.

causes.heading: Wildfire and neighboring fires
causes.body: Smoke from outside gets in through vents and gaps, leaving residue and odor with no flames inside at all.

stepsHeading: How the work goes, start to finish

steps.name: Wait for the all clear
steps.text: The US Fire Administration says not to enter until the fire department says it is safe, and not to turn utilities back on yourself.

steps.name: Call your insurer and secure the property
steps.text: Call your insurance company right away and ask what to do first. Openings get boarded up and damaged roofs tarped so weather and people stay out.

steps.name: Inspect and document
steps.text: We walk the whole house with you, photograph everything and lay out what can be cleaned, what has to come out and in what order.

steps.name: Remove the water from firefighting
steps.text: Hoses leave a lot of water behind. It is extracted and the structure dried, the same way as any water loss.

steps.name: Clean soot and treat odor
steps.text: Surfaces and contents are cleaned with methods matched to the residue, ductwork included, then the odor is treated once its source is gone.

steps.name: Rebuild
steps.text: Framing, drywall, insulation, cabinets and paint go back in, handled by the same company, so you keep one plan and one phone number.

costIntro: A fire job is priced from the walk-through, which costs you nothing. These are the things that move the number most.

costDrivers.heading: How far the smoke traveled
costDrivers.body: Smoke that went through the ductwork means cleaning rooms, closets and contents the fire never touched.

costDrivers.heading: What burned
costDrivers.body: Kitchen grease, wood and synthetic materials leave different residue, and some take more passes to clean.

costDrivers.heading: Water from the hoses
costDrivers.body: Many fire jobs are also water jobs. Wet drywall, insulation and floors add drying and removal.

costDrivers.heading: Clean or replace
costDrivers.body: Contents and materials that clean up well cost less than ones that have to be replaced, and that call is made item by item.

timeline.label: The first visit
timeline.body: Board-up or tarping, the walk-through, photos and, where there is water, extraction and drying equipment.

timeline.label: Cleaning and odor
timeline.body: Depends on how far the smoke traveled. A single room is a much shorter job than a whole house with ductwork.

timeline.label: Rebuild
timeline.body: Depends on what came out, plus permits where structural work is involved and material lead times.

insuranceBody: Call your insurer early and ask who you should talk to about cleaning and restoring your home and belongings. Photograph the damage before anything is thrown out, and let your mortgage lender or landlord know about the fire.
insuranceQuote: Save all of your receipts for any money you spend.

faqs.q: When can I go back into my house after a fire?
faqs.a: Only after the fire department says it is safe. The US Fire Administration also says not to turn gas, power or water back on yourself; let the utility or a qualified tradesperson do it.

faqs.q: The fire was only in the kitchen. Why does the whole house smell?
faqs.a: Smoke travels on air, through the HVAC system and into closets, attic insulation and other rooms. The odor comes from residue left everywhere the smoke went, so the cleanup covers more than the burned room.

faqs.q: Can you board up my house tonight?
faqs.a: Call (480) 999-3339. The line is answered 24/7, and securing the property with board-up or a roof tarp is part of fire restoration.

faqs.q: Do you deal with the water the firefighters left?
faqs.a: Yes. Water from firefighting is extracted and the structure dried as part of the job, so mold does not become a second problem.

faqs.q: Are you licensed, bonded and insured?
faqs.a: Yes. Gold Water Fire works under Arizona ROC license #264344 (KB-2), carries the license bond and is insured. IICRC certification is held on our team.

faqs.q: Will my insurance cover fire damage restoration?
faqs.a: Fire is commonly covered by homeowners policies, but your policy wording decides. Call your insurer early, photograph everything and save every receipt.
Yes. It costs nothing to have us walk the house with you and lay out what we find.

faqs.q: Do you rebuild after the cleanup?
faqs.a: Yes. Our reconstruction team, led by Construction Manager Brandon Gurr, handles framing, drywall and finish work, so the whole job stays with one company.
